newsitem.title: FRANCE: French mother punished for stealing to feed kids.
newsitem.headline: French mother punished for stealing to feed kids.

text.p: A French appeals court on Friday overturned the acquittal of a destitute single mother who stole food to feed her children in what has become a national test case.
The court imposed a symbolic 3,000 franc ($520) suspended fine on Annick G. for stealing fish and meat from three supermarkets in the western town of Poitiers.
The 36-year-old mother said she stole the food worth 1,585 francs ($276) because her monthly income of 1,827 francs ($315) did not allow her to feed her children, aged three and 19.
"I'm disappointed, I'm tired," she told reporters, sobbing. "I didn't take perfume, I didn't take anything unnecessary."

Annick had been acquitted in February on the basis of a 19th-century legal concept tolerating theft for reasons of necessity. But the state prosecutor had appealed to prevent the ruling from setting a precedent legitimising shoplifting.
